questions.stem: Which structural feature distinguishes veins from arteries when viewed in cross-section?

options.text: Veins have a larger lumen and thinner walls than arteries
Veins have thicker walls and a smaller lumen than arteries
Veins have walls that are one cell thick
Veins have more elastic tissue in their walls than arteries

questions.explanation: Veins have a relatively larger lumen and thinner walls compared to arteries because they carry blood at much lower pressure. Arteries need thick, elastic walls to withstand the high pressure from the heart.
